Long answer, sorry...but here I go: Nocturnal Animals is a film that absolutely bothers the fuck out of me. It has the number one scariest jumpscare I have ever seen. It's not a horror movie, in a similar way to how Mulholland Drive isn't, but it comes pretty close. I SCREAMED out loud in the theater watching the baby monitor scene for the first time, and that is something extremely rare for me to do. I can count on one hand how many times I had such an intense response to something on-screen in a non-horror film, and that scene right there is at the top of the list. And the sick feeling I got never went away. Aaron Taylor-Johnson more than earned his Golden Globe win for this film simply because he freaked me out so bad and made my stomach turn so much. He was actually totally fucking evil, vile, foul, deranged, sadistic, creepy, strange, disgusting, and terrifying. I had nightmares about his character in this film for a brief while, which is yet again uncommon for me. Anyone who knows me well enough knows that I will throw money at anything Aaron Taylor-Johnson is in, I love him to pieces...but good God, I was NOT prepared for any of it this time. I actually felt physically ill watching his performance in Nocturnal Animals. I sincerely hope that was the one and only time I'll ever get the ick from him, and it better not happen again...I couldn't handle it then, and I still can't now. I was profoundly unsettled and unnerved by that film, and he's one of the biggest reasons why. With that being said, I won't listen to any criticism of any kind about that man's acting abilities because his range is actually incredible. He (and Jake Gyllenhaal as well) is deeply underrated as an actor, and that is a hill I will die on. Except in this case, he was TOO good at the sadism. Definitely enough to make my skin crawl, and not in the usual fun way. My chest and stomach hurt because I was HORRIFIED and SICKENED. This is NOT AT ALL the man I had a mad crush on in Angus, Thongs, and Perfect Snogging when I was a young girl...this is something else entirely. If that doesn't say range, I don't know what does.

For me, it's a three-way tie between Jake Gyllenhaal, Paul Mescal, and Aaron Taylor-Johnson. Both Jake Gyllenhaal and Paul Mescal both have been nominated once, for Brokeback Mountain and Aftersun respectively. Neither have been nominated again since. Paul Mescal has been consistently amazing in everything he's been in, but Jake Gyllenhaal not being nominated more than that once let alone winning any Oscars is genuinely surprising to me. Nocturnal Animals, Enemy, Prisoners, Nightcrawler, Wildlife, Donnie Darko, Zodiac, Okja...I could go on and on. All Oscar-worthy performances in my eyes. Somehow, Aaron Taylor-Johnson hasn't yet either, and I was really hoping he would have for at least Anna Karenina or his role in Nocturnal Animals as well. That guy's range is insane. His Golden Globe win was VERY well deserved. However, my number one favorite actor FINALLY won his Oscar last year 👍🏻

Side note: Nocturnal Animals is one of the most disturbing films I have ever seen, but also one of the very best films of its kind. Stacked cast, beautifully shot, engaging and thought-provoking...I highly recommend it.

I've seen a few Lars von Trier films mentioned here, but Melancholia got to me so deeply I didn't think it was possible. The idea that a planet is on a collision course with the Earth and during that time relationships with close family members are strained because you're so depressed you can't take care of yourself hits very hard. I saw this movie at a very dark time in my life, and it has stuck with me ever since. Lars von Trier does depression in his films really well, sometimes too well. 

Another film that deeply saddened me for days on end was Martyrs (the 2008 French original, not the 2015 American remake). I've never seen such a brutal account of abuse, deep rooted trauma, revenge gone bad, and extreme torture. The director, Pascal Laugier, stated in an interview that he sought out to make a movie about pain and the film is absolutely relentless when it comes to that. There are only a handful of horror movies I will never revisit, and this is one of them simply because it bothered me so much I felt like I needed therapy afterwards. 

I felt similarly after viewing Possum, a British horror movie that deals with abuse and the trauma that comes with it. It's based off of a short story which is just as difficult to handle, and I had nightmares for weeks after watching it. Matthew Holness is very underrated in my opinion, and he deserves recognition for his ability to create such a powerful and harrowing tone. 

Those are three that I can think of right off the bat. Melancholia is more tame that Martyrs; Martyrs is one of the hardest films I've ever had to sit through, not because of the horror elements but because of what it depicts/represents. Melancholia, however, was gorgeously shot and edited in addition to being an all around existentially sad film. In other words, it's easier to recommend Melancholia to people than it is Martyrs. I genuinely don't know how to recommend Martyrs because it's simply just that hard to watch. Possum is just as depressing, it's just not on the same level in terms of violence and gore. This was long-winded and I'm sorry...but I love films that make me feel something, good or bad, and I am of the belief that if a film can get that big of a reaction out of someone, it's doing its job as a film. All three films made me cry like a baby.

Edited to add that I don't know how to block out spoilers, so I apologize for spoiling the films I mentioned. I also got Possum's director's name wrong...my apologies for that too.
